title: Arithmetic lifts and semilinear paths of finite fibre functors
statement:
Let $K$ be a perfect field (every algebraic extension of $K$ is separable), let $L$ be an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $Y_0$ be a separated finite-type $K$-scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Put $Y=Y_0\times_K L$ [def-pc-base-change], assume $Y$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], and choose a geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. Write $\bar y_0$ for its composite with $Y\to Y_0$ and $i:L\hookrightarrow\Omega$ for its map of constants. Use the finite etale categories of [def-galois-categories], and let $F=F_{\bar y}$ and $F_0=F_{\bar y_0}$ be their fibre functors [def-galois-fibre-functor]. The structure maps induce homomorphisms as in [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality], and give an exact sequence of profinite groups
$$
1\longrightarrow P:=\operatorname{Aut}(F)\xrightarrow{j}G:=\operatorname{Aut}(F_0)\xrightarrow{r}\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)\longrightarrow1.
$$
Give $\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$ its inverse-limit topology over the finite Galois subextensions of $L/K$. Here $r$ is characterized on the finite constant covers $Y_0\times_K\operatorname{Spec}E$, for finite subextensions $K\subseteq E\subseteq L$, by the action $\tau\mapsto r(g)\circ\tau$ on $\operatorname{Hom}_K(E,L)$, identified with their geometric fibres using $i$. Identify $P$ with its image under $j$.

For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$ put $h_\sigma=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma):Y\to Y$. The set $r^{-1}(\sigma)$ is canonically in bijection with the natural isomorphisms
$$
\lambda_s:F_{h_\sigma\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\bar y}.
$$
The bijection is specified by the following evaluation rule, which fixes its inverse convention. For any finite intermediate extension $E/K$ and finite etale cover $Q_E\to Y_E=Y_0\times_KE$, let $Q=Q_E\times_E L$ and let
$$
\iota_\sigma:F_{h_\sigma\bar y}(Q)\hookrightarrow F_0(Q_E),\qquad
\iota_1:F_{\bar y}(Q)\hookrightarrow F_0(Q_E)
$$
be the injections obtained by forgetting the $L$-structure. The image of $\iota_\sigma$ is the fibre of $Q_E\to Y_0$ whose map of constants $E\to\Omega$ is $i\circ\sigma|_E$, and the image of $\iota_1$ has map of constants $i|_E$. Regard $Q_E\to Y_0$ as a finite etale cover. For every $z\in F_{h_\sigma\bar y}(Q)$,
$$
 \iota_1(\lambda_{s,Q}(z))=s^{-1}\cdot\iota_\sigma(z).
$$
This rule is independent of the chosen finite model, and applies to all finite etale $Y$-covers and their morphisms. Via the canonical first-projection identification $F_{\bar y}(h_\sigma^*Q)\cong F_{h_\sigma\bar y}(Q)$ for base change [def-pc-base-change], the resulting bijections satisfy
$$
 \lambda_{s,Q}(g\cdot z)=(s^{-1}gs)\cdot\lambda_{s,Q}(z)\qquad(g\in P).
$$
On the left, $P$ acts on $F_{\bar y}(h_\sigma^*Q)$ by evaluation of the fibre functor; on the right it acts on $F_{\bar y}(Q)$. For $a\in P$,
$$
 \lambda_{as,Q}=\lambda_{s,Q}\circ a^{-1}_{h_\sigma^*Q}.
$$
Under the equivalence with finite locally constant sheaves of sets [thm-galois-lc-etale], these are the same natural isomorphisms of stalk functors and the same identities. No coefficient module, descent isomorphism or Weil group is part of this statement.

source.place: Tag 0BTX, lemma-ses-field (exact sequence and descent to finite separable subextensions); Tag 0BTV, lemma-limit (objects, morphisms and eventual equalities in finite etale covers); Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (fibre-functor actions), and Tag 0BNE, lemma-fundamental-group-Galois-group (Galois action on embeddings). The displayed semilinear-path correspondence and normalization are an agent formulation of those finite-fibre constructions, matching the pointed-universal-cover action of Weil II (1.1.12), p.152.
